subject: Learning Methods
title: Light Sleep: Stage One and Two
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Light Sleep: Stage One and Two.

hook.text: You spend half your night in stage two light sleep. It isn't wasted time. It contains learning-boosting sleep spindles.

buildup.text: Sleep spindles are brief bursts of brain activity lasting one to two seconds. They occur hundreds of times each night.

discovery.text: Spindles transfer information from the hippocampus to the cortex. They move today's learning into long-term storage.

twist.text: People who produce more sleep spindles score higher on memory tests. Spindle count predicts learning capacity better.

climax.text: Protect your full sleep, including the light stages. Every phase contributes to consolidating what you studied.

punchline.text: Sleep spindles move learning into long-term storage. Every stage counts.

quiz.question: What role do sleep spindles play in learning?
options: They wake you up to prevent oversleeping
They transfer information from hippocampus to cortex for long-term storage
They eliminate unnecessary memories to free space
